title: Flow cytometry analysis of diatoms and coccolithophores with diagnostic stains (via a BD Biosciences Accuri C6)
author: Jozef Nissimov
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d9i94d

steps.title: Set instrument orifice
steps.instruction: Select the 70 µm orifice on the BD Accuri C6, which is appropriate for cells sized ~5–10 µm.

steps.title: Create preliminary chlorophyll plot
steps.instruction: Load an unstained control sample, set a threshold, and generate a plot with FL3‑H (chlorophyll) on the Y‑axis and SSC‑H on the X‑axis, both displayed in log scale.

steps.title: Define chlorophyll quadrants
steps.instruction: Add a vertical line to the FL3‑H vs SSC‑H plot to separate positive (above the line) from negative (below) chlorophyll fluorescence, thereby dividing the plot into four quadrants.

steps.title: Gate positive fluorescence population
steps.instruction: Select the top two quadrants (upper left and upper right) with a square gate to create population R1, ensuring the zoom view is set to ‘all the way out’ and noting the horizontal line that defines the gate.

steps.title: Create size‑based plot for R1
steps.instruction: Generate a new plot with FL3‑H (chlorophyll) on the Y‑axis and FSC‑H on the X‑axis, both in log scale, and restrict the data to gate R1 from the previous plot.

steps.title: Apply size gate
steps.instruction: Add a vertical line at FSC‑H = 5.6 × 10⁵; events to the right of this line correspond to cells larger than ~1 µm. This divides the plot into quadrants for size discrimination.

steps.title: Create diagnostic fluorescence plot
steps.instruction: Set up a new plot with FL1‑H (green fluorescence) on the Y‑axis and FSC‑H on the X‑axis, both in log scale. In the gate options, choose the quadrant‑marker mode and include the upper‑right quadrant (Q2‑UR) from the previous size‑based plot (R1).

steps.title: Define stained vs unstained quadrants
steps.instruction: On the FL1‑H vs FSC‑H plot, add a vertical cutoff line; the unstained population should fall in the bottom‑right quadrant below this line, which separates negatively from positively stained cells.
